$comment: Project-scoped MCP servers. Claude Code picks this up when you run `claude`
inside a clone of this repo, and asks you to approve each server first.
Keys are read from your shell environment via ${VAR} — never stored here.
Both are third-party community packages, pinned to verified npm versions.
Verified by actually running them in a cloud session:
* ${PWD} expands to the directory you launched `claude` from, not the repo
root. Images land in <that dir>/previews, and each server REFUSES to write
anywhere outside it. Launch claude from the repo root, or set the *_OUTPUT_DIR
* A server with no key still starts, then fails on the first call — except
gemini-mcp, which closes the connection outright. A missing GEMINI_API_KEY
* From a CLOUD Claude Code session api.openai.com is blocked by the network
egress proxy ('Host not in allowlist'), so openai-image only works locally.
generativelanguage.googleapis.com IS reachable there, so gemini-image works
in both places once a key exists.
